title: Improved flame retardancy and mechanical properties of bacterial cellulose fabrics via solvent exchange and entrapment of zein and gluten
treatment_chemistry: zein,20 wt% relative to original BC
treatment_method: Original kombucha BC was washed, bleached and swollen according to cited protocols; exact upstream recipe not repeated in this article. Immerse wet pretreated BC in 80% v/v ethanol at 25 C for 24 h. Dissolve 20 wt% zein relative to BC in 80% ethanol at 1:10 w/v BC:liquor; ultrasound 25 C for 30 min. Immerse solvent-exchanged BC; ultrasound 25 C for 30 min; shake 80 rpm at 30 C for 1 h; dry 25 C for 24 h.
TG_locator: TGA analysis prose p 9, Figure 6: exact residue percentages at 1000 C.
LOI_locator: LOI analysis prose pp 9-10: exact own LOI25 and 50.
conditions_locator: Flame-retardant properties methods p 3; preparation pp 2-3; optimization pp 4-5 identifies 20 wt% zein and 40 wt% gluten.
pairing_evidence: Methods and optimization explicitly define final BC-zein-SE and BC-gluten-E preparations; thermal and LOI prose use those same codes. Other screening loadings lack matched own LOI and remain excluded.
source_location: Original final publisher PDF, 16 pages; methods/preparation pp 2-5 and thermal/LOI pp 9-10.
limitations: Complete original publisher article reviewed. Exact final 1000 C residual masses are source prose values, not curve estimates or R800. OriginalBC own LOI19 and cowhideLOI30 are reported without matched exact TG values, so excluded. Optimization dose series lacks matchedLOI; no extra inferred states. Prewashing/bleaching/swelling is preparation, not durability washing. TG start temperature and mass not reported. Paper describes driedBC as a leather-substitute textile made of nanofibrous sheets; do not relabel it woven fabric.
